avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction reduces exemestane bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concomitant use; counsel patient to discontinue prior to exemestane initiation

avoid_supplements.name: Red Clover (Trifolium pratense)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Phytoestrogen content may antagonize exemestane's estrogen-suppressing effects
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; recommend alternative supplements without estrogenic activity

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit Seed Extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition may increase exemestane exposure
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased side effects; limit grapefruit product consumption

caution_supplements.name: Black Cohosh
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential weak estrogenic activity may modestly reduce efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor clinical response and consider alternatives

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit Juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase exemestane plasma concentrations
caution_foods.action: Limit or avoid regular consumption; educate patient on potential for increased exposure

monitoring_notes: Exemestane is a prodrug requiring hepatic metabolism for activation; monitor for efficacy loss with CYP3A4 inducers and for tolerability with potent inhibitors. Counsel on avoidance of phytoestrogens and estrogenic supplements to maintain therapeutic efficacy in breast cancer treatment.
